name: Tabs
summary: A row of buttons over a box of content is the easiest thing on a page to draw and one of the easiest to get wrong. The pattern hands the arrow keys a job the Tab key used to do, so the whole strip becomes one stop — and the panel underneath still has to be somewhere the keyboard can land.
demoNote: Examples 2 to 5 are live. Example 2 asks the browser which elements it will really give focus to and prints every stop three strips have; example 3 counts the panels opened while arrowing across; example 4 names the next thing Tab reaches after the selected tab; example 5 puts a row of links wearing role=tab beside the same links in a nav.
